introduction: This spec makes the SDK's subprocess runner (`tools.Run`, `tools.RunArgv`) a complete embedder-facing process runner. It adds standard input, a choice of keeping the head or the tail of the output, a log file the caller names, the credential-stripped environment by default and a pinned outcome contract with an `IOErr` field. It also carries the `core.ToolMetadata` every tool handler already computes onto `core.ToolResultMessage` and `AfterToolCallContext`. From there the metadata reaches events, stop policies, run results, the session log and resumed agents, and it never reaches a provider request.

glossary.ExecOptions: The options struct of tools.Run and tools.RunArgv (Dir, Timeout, MaxBytes, KeepHead, SpillDir, LogPath, Stdin, Env, DrainIdle, DrainCeiling).
glossary.ExecResult: The value tools.Run and tools.RunArgv return for a started process: Output, Outcome, ExitCode, Truncated, TotalBytes, SpillPath, Duration and IOErr.
glossary.IOErr: The ExecResult field reporting a failure to move bytes between the caller and the process (stdin read, log or spill write, Wait I/O completion) that did not stop the process.
glossary.Outcome: tools.Outcome, one of ok, exit, signal, timeout or abort, classified by ClassifyOutcome with the precedence abort > timeout > signal > exit.
glossary.handler-less result: A tool result finalized without running a tool's Execute function: unknown tool, invalid arguments, BeforeToolCall block, plugin block, batch abort, max_tokens synthesis, the no_result backstop, and provider.RepairTranscript's synthetic results.
glossary.head-mode marker: The Accumulator's TruncateHead marker, appended after the retained bytes: `[N bytes elided of T total. Full output: PATH]`, without the path clause when there is no file.
glossary.non-empty metadata: A *core.ToolMetadata that is non-nil and has at least one field set: a non-zero scalar, or a non-nil ExitCode pointer.
glossary.post-exit drain: The re-arming idle read of the shared output pipe after the child exits, bounded by DrainIdle and DrainCeiling (REQ-TOOL-17.5).
glossary.process tree: The child process and every process it starts. It runs in its own process group on unix (Setpgid) and is killed with taskkill /T on Windows.
glossary.request goldens: testdata/golden/request_{anthropic,openai,openai_responses,google,ollama}.json, the byte-exact wire bodies golden_requests_test.go builds from canonicalRequest.
glossary.session codec: session.EncodeMessage / session.DecodeMessage (encodeMessage/decodeMessage in session/codec.go). It is the lossless message encoding used by the session log and, through core.MarshalEvent, by the event JSON union.
glossary.spill file: The temporary file in SpillDir into which the Accumulator writes the complete output on first write.

requirements.title: Standard input for the runner
requirements.rationale: An embedder's verifier and phase runner must feed a program its input without falling back to a hand-written exec.CommandContext runner that has no process-group kill.

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.Stdin is nil
criteria.action: give the child the null device as its standard input, as before this change
criteria.contract: A child that reads stdin sees end-of-file at once; Outcome and Output are unchanged from the pre-change behaviour

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.Stdin is a non-nil io.Reader
criteria.action: copy the reader into the child's standard input through a pipe the runner owns, and close the child's standard input when the reader returns io.EOF
criteria.contract: A child that copies stdin to stdout produces Output byte-identical to the reader's content; IOErr is nil

criteria.condition: the child exits or closes its standard input before reading all of the reader's bytes
criteria.action: stop copying, treat the unread input as no error, and classify Outcome from the exit status
criteria.contract: Returned error is nil; IOErr is nil; Outcome is ok when the child exited 0

criteria.condition: the Stdin reader returns an error other than io.EOF
criteria.action: close the child's standard input and record the read error in ExecResult.IOErr whatever the child's exit status, classifying Outcome from the exit status
criteria.contract: Returned error is nil; errors.Is(res.IOErr, readerErr) is true for both a zero and a non-zero exit; Outcome is ok or exit from the wait status

criteria.condition: the child has exited and the post-exit drain has finished
criteria.guard: the Stdin reader is still blocked in Read
criteria.action: return the ExecResult without waiting for the reader, and end the stdin copier goroutine when the reader's Read returns
criteria.contract: The call returns within DrainIdle plus scheduling slack of the child's exit; no copier goroutine remains after the blocked reader is unblocked

requirements.title: Which end of the output is kept
requirements.rationale: A caller reading a test log or a report wants its beginning, while every existing caller relies on tail truncation as the zero value.

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.KeepHead is false (the zero value)
criteria.action: keep the last MaxBytes bytes of the output preceded by the tail-mode marker, exactly as before this change
criteria.contract: Output is byte-identical to the pre-change Output for the same command and MaxBytes

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.KeepHead is true
criteria.guard: the process writes more than the effective MaxBytes bytes
criteria.action: keep the first MaxBytes bytes of the output followed by the Accumulator's head-mode marker, which names the elided byte count, the total and the spill or log path when one exists
criteria.contract: Output == first MaxBytes bytes + "\n[E bytes elided of T total. Full output: P]" with P present only when a spill or log file exists; Truncated is true

criteria.action: treat MaxBytes <= 0 as DefaultByteLimit (50 KB) in both head and tail mode
for any output byte sequence and any MaxBytes, report the same TotalBytes (every byte the process wrote) and the same Truncated (TotalBytes exceeds the retained window) in head mode as in tail mode

criteria.condition: the process writes exactly MaxBytes bytes
criteria.action: return the whole output with no marker in both modes
criteria.contract: Truncated is false; Output equals the bytes written; TotalBytes == MaxBytes

requirements.title: A caller-named log of the full output
requirements.rationale: An embedder needs the complete output in a file it chose, and needs to know before the run starts if it cannot have one.

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.LogPath is set
criteria.action: write the complete interleaved stdout and stderr to that file as it arrives, independent of truncation
criteria.contract: After the call the file's content is byte-identical to the full output, including when Output is truncated; TotalBytes equals the file size

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.LogPath is a relative path
criteria.action: resolve it against ExecOptions.Dir, or against the process working directory when Dir is empty
criteria.contract: ExecResult.SpillPath is the absolute resolved path, and the file exists there

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.LogPath is set and the call is about to start the process
criteria.action: create missing parent directories with mode 0o700 and create or truncate the log file with mode 0o600 before starting the process
criteria.contract: On unix the created directories have permission bits 0o700 and the file 0o600; a pre-existing file's old content is gone

criteria.condition: the LogPath file or its parent directory cannot be created or opened
criteria.action: return an error without starting the process
criteria.contract: Returns (ExecResult{}, non-nil error); a marker file the command would have created does not exist

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.LogPath is set
criteria.action: use the log file in place of SpillDir for that call, creating no temporary spill file, and report the absolute log path in SpillPath, including when the command printed nothing, and in the truncation marker
criteria.contract: SpillDir contains no agentkit-exec-*.log file after the call; SpillPath == absolute LogPath for a command with empty output; a truncated Output's marker names the log path

criteria.condition: writing to the log file or to a SpillDir spill file fails after the process has started
criteria.action: stop writing to that file, leave the process running to completion, keep accumulating Output, and record the write error in ExecResult.IOErr
criteria.contract: Returned error is nil; IOErr is non-nil; Outcome is classified from the exit status; Output holds the retained window

criteria.action: never delete a LogPath file, whatever the Outcome
criteria.contract: The log file exists after calls ending in ok, exit, signal, timeout and abort

requirements.title: The reduced environment by default
requirements.rationale: The runner's nil environment inherited every credential in the process, while tools.Options already defaults to ReducedEnv (REQ-SEC-08).

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.Env is nil
criteria.action: run the child with ReducedEnv(nil)
criteria.contract: A credential variable set in the test process (for example AGENTKIT_TEST_API_KEY) is absent from the child's environment; PATH and HOME are present verbatim

criteria.condition: ExecOptions.Env is non-nil, including an empty slice
criteria.action: pass it to the child verbatim, with no variable added or removed
criteria.contract: A child given Env {"FOO=1"} sees FOO=1 and no credential variable from the parent; os.Environ() passed as Env exposes the parent's credential variables

criteria.action: resolve a bare program name through the PATH of the environment the child runs with, so a nil Env resolves the same binary as the process PATH because ReducedEnv keeps PATH verbatim

requirements.title: The outcome and error contract
requirements.rationale: An embedder must tell a timeout from its own cancellation from a failed or successful exit without parsing text, and must never see an I/O failure reported as a clean exit 0.

criteria.action: for any call that starts a process, return a nil error and an ExecResult whose Outcome is exactly one of ok, exit, signal, timeout or abort, classified from the state at the moment the child exited

criteria.condition: the caller's ctx is cancelled while the child is running
criteria.action: kill the whole process tree, grandchildren included, and classify the call as abort
criteria.contract: Outcome == OutcomeAbort; Duration is measured to the child's exit; a grandchild that would create a marker file after the kill never creates it

criteria.condition: the deadline derived from ExecOptions.Timeout expires while the caller's ctx is not done
criteria.action: kill the whole process tree, grandchildren included, and classify the call as timeout
criteria.contract: Outcome == OutcomeTimeout; Duration >= Timeout and is measured to the child's exit; a grandchild that would create a marker file after the kill never creates it

criteria.condition: the caller's own ctx deadline, shorter than ExecOptions.Timeout, expires while the child is running
criteria.action: kill the whole process tree and classify the call as abort, not timeout
criteria.contract: Outcome == OutcomeAbort

criteria.condition: the child exits on its own and the caller's ctx is cancelled later, during the post-exit drain
criteria.action: keep the outcome classified at the child's exit
criteria.contract: Outcome is ok or exit from the wait status, never abort

criteria.condition: the child exits before any deadline or cancellation
criteria.action: classify the outcome as signal, exit or ok from the wait status and report the exit status in ExitCode, using 128+signum for a signal-killed child on unix
criteria.contract: exit 0 → (ok, 0); exit 3 → (exit, 3); killed by SIGTERM on unix → (signal, 143)

criteria.condition: the call cannot start a process because argv is empty, the program is not found, LogPath cannot be opened, or creating a pipe or forking fails
criteria.action: return an error and run nothing; no other condition returns a non-nil error
criteria.contract: Returns (ExecResult{}, non-nil error) for exactly these start failures

criteria.condition: cmd.Wait returns an error that is neither an exit status nor a signal, such as exec.ErrWaitDelay
criteria.action: record that error in ExecResult.IOErr instead of discarding it, and classify Outcome from the exit status
criteria.contract: Returned error is nil; errors.Is(res.IOErr, waitErr) is true; IOErr is nil on every call where no stdin, log, spill or Wait I/O failure occurred

requirements.title: The built-in shell tools are unchanged
requirements.rationale: The runner's new options are for embedders; the model's execute, run_command and powershell tools must produce byte-identical results.

criteria.action: call tools.Run or tools.RunArgv with their explicit Options.Env, KeepHead false, MaxBytes DefaultByteLimit and Options.SpillDir, and with Stdin nil and LogPath empty

criteria.condition: a model command run by execute, run_command or powershell reads standard input
criteria.action: give it the null device (REQ-TOOL-06)
criteria.contract: The command sees end-of-file at once and does not block

criteria.action: produce ToolResult.Text, the status line, Data, Error and Metadata byte-identical to the pre-change values for every ExecResult with the same Output, Outcome, ExitCode, Truncated, TotalBytes, SpillPath and Duration

criteria.condition: the ExecResult a shell tool receives has a non-nil IOErr
criteria.action: leave the IOErr out of the tool result
criteria.contract: Text, Data, Error and Metadata equal those of the same ExecResult with IOErr nil

criteria.action: pass the existing tests in tools/tools_test.go and tools/reqtool06_test.go with no edit to either file

requirements.title: Tool metadata on the result message
requirements.rationale: An embedder reads exit code, outcome and truncation from the transcript record rather than parsing `[exit N]` out of model-facing text.

criteria.condition: a tool's Execute function returns a ToolResult whose Metadata is non-empty metadata
criteria.action: set core.ToolResultMessage.Metadata to a copy of that metadata owned by the message, with its own ExitCode pointer
criteria.contract: msg.Metadata is equal by value to the handler's Metadata; msg.Metadata != handler pointer; msg.Metadata.ExitCode != handler ExitCode pointer when non-nil

criteria.action: for any tool that reuses one ToolMetadata value or ExitCode pointer across calls, including in a parallel batch, keep each message's Metadata unchanged when the tool later mutates that value

criteria.condition: a tool's Execute function returns a ToolResult whose Metadata is nil, or non-nil with every field zero and ExitCode nil
criteria.action: leave ToolResultMessage.Metadata nil
criteria.contract: msg.Metadata == nil

criteria.condition: a result comes from a Handler-style tool, from a handler panic, or is a handler-less result (unknown tool, invalid arguments, BeforeToolCall block, plugin block, batch abort, max_tokens synthesis, the no_result backstop, or a provider.RepairTranscript synthetic result)
criteria.system: batch executor, agent loop and provider.RepairTranscript
criteria.action: produce the ToolResultMessage with nil Metadata
criteria.contract: msg.Metadata == nil; Content, IsError and the emitted events are unchanged from the pre-change values

criteria.action: deep-copy Metadata, including a fresh ExitCode pointer, so that mutating the clone's metadata leaves the original unchanged

criteria.condition: a tool call whose handler returned non-empty metadata is finalized
criteria.action: expose that metadata on the message in ToolResultEvent.Message, TurnEndEvent.ToolResults, StopContext.ToolResults, the agent's History and RunResult.Messages
criteria.contract: Each of the five carries a Metadata equal by value to the handler's, for example ExitCode 2 and Outcome "exit" from a failing execute call

criteria.action: build ToolResultMessage.Content from ToolResult.LLMText and Blocks as before, leaving ToolResult.ToLLMMap and LLMText unchanged, so Content is byte-identical whether or not Metadata is set

requirements.title: The handler's result reaches AfterToolCall
requirements.rationale: A post-tool hook needs the structured result the handler produced, while the message stays the one record that is emitted and persisted.

criteria.condition: AfterToolCall is configured and a tool handler has run
criteria.action: pass core.AfterToolCallContext.ToolResult as the handler's result by value, after panic and Handler-error conversion, and pass Result as the already built *ToolResultMessage carrying its Metadata
criteria.contract: in.ToolResult equals the handler's returned ToolResult; in.Result.Metadata equals by value in.ToolResult.Metadata when that is non-empty

criteria.condition: an AfterToolCall hook edits in.Result.Metadata
criteria.action: use the edited metadata in the emitted ToolResultEvent, the persisted session entry, StopContext.ToolResults and history
criteria.contract: All four carry the hook's edited value

criteria.condition: an AfterToolCall hook modifies its in.ToolResult copy, including fields reached through its Metadata pointer
criteria.action: leave the emitted, persisted and stop-policy message unchanged
criteria.contract: The ToolResultEvent message equals the message the batch built before the hook

criteria.condition: a tool handler panics and AfterToolCall is configured
criteria.action: pass the panic-converted result in ToolResult and a Result with nil Metadata
criteria.contract: in.ToolResult.Error == "panic"; in.Result.Metadata == nil

criteria.action: keep the REQ-TOOL-13.3 termination-vote rules and the image normalization after the hook unchanged

requirements.title: Metadata is persisted and never sent to the model
requirements.rationale: Metadata has to survive the session log, event JSON and resume, and the model's request bytes must stay identical.

criteria.condition: a tool_result message with non-empty metadata is encoded
criteria.action: write a `metadata` object after `usage` and before `timestamp`, keyed by ToolMetadata's JSON tag names in declaration order (truncated, truncated_by, total_bytes, total_lines, spill_path, duration_ms, exit_code, outcome, line_ending), omitting zero fields and writing exit_code whenever ExitCode is non-nil, including 0
criteria.contract: testdata/golden/session_log.jsonl differs from its previous content only by one metadata object on the tool_result line written by golden_test.go

criteria.action: for any ToolResultMessage whose Metadata is nil or non-empty, decode the encoding back to a message whose Metadata is equal by value (nil stays nil, ExitCode 0 stays a pointer to 0), and re-encode the decoded message to the same bytes

criteria.condition: a tool_result entry is decoded whose `metadata` key is absent or holds an object with no known field
criteria.action: decode Metadata as nil, drop unknown keys nested inside a metadata object, and keep `metadata` in toolResultKnown so it never lands in Unknown
criteria.contract: msg.Metadata == nil for absent or all-unknown metadata; msg.Unknown has no `metadata` key

criteria.condition: a session log written before this change, with no metadata key, is loaded
criteria.action: read every tool result back with nil Metadata and re-encode the log byte-identically, writing metadata only as a top-level key of the tool_result object so a build without this change keeps it in Unknown
criteria.contract: Decoded Metadata is nil; re-encoded bytes equal the input bytes

criteria.condition: session.EventJSON encodes a ToolResultEvent, TurnEndEvent or AgentDoneEvent containing a tool result with non-empty metadata
criteria.action: include the same metadata object in the encoded message, through session.EncodeMessage
criteria.contract: The message JSON inside the event carries a metadata object byte-identical to the session log's for the same message

criteria.condition: NewAgentFromSession resumes a session whose tool_result entries carry metadata
criteria.action: restore the metadata into the agent's history
criteria.contract: Agent.History() tool results carry Metadata equal by value to the values recorded before the restart

criteria.condition: the Anthropic, OpenAI chat, OpenAI responses, Google or Ollama encoder builds a request whose history holds a tool result with populated Metadata
criteria.action: emit a request body containing nothing derived from Metadata
criteria.contract: With canonicalRequest's tool result carrying a populated Metadata, the five request goldens stay byte-identical

criteria.action: compute the same estimate for a ToolResultMessage whether or not its Metadata is set

requirements.title: Documentation and module policy
requirements.rationale: The steering rules treat stale docs as regressions, and the root module must stay standard-library-only and cgo-free.

criteria.action: contain a subsection titled "Subprocess runner (`tools.Run`, `tools.RunArgv`)" with an ExecOptions table listing Dir, Timeout, MaxBytes, KeepHead, SpillDir, LogPath, Stdin, Env, DrainIdle and DrainCeiling, and the ExecResult fields with the Outcome rules and IOErr
state in its `BeforeToolCall`, `AfterToolCall` row that AfterToolCall receives the handler's ToolResult and that ToolResultMessage.Metadata carries the tool's metadata
mention the metadata in the finalize step of the data flow and name RunArgv as the embedder's process runner in the `tools` package row

contain a new erratum file prefixed `04_` recording the departures from docs/prd/06 §6 and §9: RunArgv instead of Exec, Outcome instead of TimedOut/Aborted, no ExitCode -1, KeepHead instead of KeepTail, no WaitDelay option. It also records that §7 and §5's usage and abort items were already implemented
stay standard-library-only and cgo-free, with go.mod gaining no require line and the internal/policy tests and `make check` passing

execution_paths.title: An embedder runs a verifier with stdin, a named log and head truncation

steps.action: calls tools.RunArgv(ctx, argv, ExecOptions{Dir, Stdin: reader, LogPath: "logs/verify.log", KeepHead: true, MaxBytes: small, Timeout}) with a nil Env
resolves the program through the PATH of ReducedEnv(nil), resolves LogPath against Dir, creates the parent directory 0o700 and the log file 0o600 before starting anything
starts the child in its own process group, copies the reader into the child's stdin and closes it at io.EOF
reads its input, writes more than MaxBytes bytes to the shared output pipe and exits with status 2
writes every output byte to the log file and keeps the first MaxBytes bytes in Output, followed by the head-mode marker naming the log path
receives ExecResult{Outcome: exit, ExitCode: 2, Truncated: true, SpillPath: absolute log path, IOErr: nil} and reads the complete output from the log file

execution_paths.title: Timeout and cancellation kill the process tree and are told apart

steps.action: calls tools.RunArgv with ExecOptions.Timeout on a command that starts a background grandchild, which would create a marker file later, and then sleeps past the timeout
detects that the Timeout-derived deadline expired while the caller's ctx is live, and kills the whole process group
terminates the child and the grandchild before the marker file is created
returns ExecResult{Outcome: timeout} with Duration measured to the child's exit
runs the same command with a ctx it cancels, and with a ctx deadline shorter than Timeout, and receives Outcome abort both times with no marker file created

execution_paths.title: Tool metadata reaches every observer and the session log but never the provider

steps.action: returns an assistant turn calling the execute tool with a command that exits 2
runs the execute handler, which calls tools.Run and returns a ToolResult whose Metadata carries ExitCode 2 and Outcome exit
builds the ToolResultMessage with its own copy of the Metadata and calls AfterToolCall with the handler's ToolResult and the message
emits ToolResultEvent and TurnEndEvent and calls the stop policy, each carrying the message with its Metadata
writes the tool_result entry with a metadata object between usage and timestamp
builds the next request body from the message Content only, with no metadata in the bytes
resumes the session with NewAgentFromSession and reads ExitCode 2 and Outcome exit from the restored history's tool result
